summary.summary: Torfaen's treasury year was quiet and compliant: external debt fell £8.2m to £123.4m (all fixed rate, average 4.20%), financing costs are just 3.54% of net revenue, and borrowing sits within its £129.1m capital financing requirement and £150.7m authorised limit. The council took no new long-term borrowing while rates were high, instead rolling temporary loans from other councils — £30m outstanding at year end with an average remaining life of about a month at 5.34% — a deliberate wait-for-rates-to-fall stance it says it will unwind when there is a financial case. The only indicator exceeded was investment interest-rate exposure (£187,000 sensitivity vs £150,000 assumed), which worked in the council's favour, and investments of £16.5m stayed above the £10m MIFID II floor throughout.

signals.headline: £40.9m of £123.4m fixed-rate debt matures within 12 months of 31 March 2026 (limit £61.7m/50%), including £30m of temporary local-authority loans with 0.08 years average life at 5.34%
signals.why: Roughly a quarter of the debt book rolls over on a near-monthly basis at rates above the council's 3.53% PWLB average until long-term rates fall — modest in scale but a live dependency on the inter-authority lending market.

signals.headline: All key 2025/26 prudential indicators met: financing costs 3.54% of net revenue vs 3.59% estimate, gross borrowing £123.4m within the £129.1m CFR, £150.728m authorised limit never breached, debt down £8.2m in year
signals.why: Core affordability and compliance are verified sound; the one exceeded indicator (investment interest-rate exposure) increased income rather than cost.

findings.headline: Joanne Griffiths has been appointed Head of Pensions, succeeding Alex Bull, who left the Fund in March
findings.detail: The Chair's foreword records that Alex Bull left the Fund in March to join the WPP Investment Management Company, and congratulates Joanne Griffiths on her appointment as the Fund's new Head of Pensions.
findings.matters: A change of senior pensions officer is relevant to finance directors at other councils, both as a governance change and as a point of continuity for pooling and valuation work.
findings.quote: congratulate Joanne Griffiths on her appointment as the Fund

findings.paper_title: Agenda Item 05 - Appendix 1 - Draft Annual Report & Accounts 2025 2026
findings.headline: The Local Pension Board reports that the McCloud implementation deadline may be extended to 31st August 2026
findings.detail: The Board was consulted on the discretion to extend the deadline for completing the McCloud implementation to 31st August 2026. The paper describes McCloud as a complex national LGPS administration project.
findings.matters: Finance and pensions teams at other councils working on the same national McCloud remedy can compare their own completion dates with the extended deadline.
findings.figures: Deadline for McCloud implementation extended to 31st August 2026 (discretion under consultation)
findings.quote: discretion to extend the deadline for completing the McCloud implementation to 31st August 2026

findings.paper_title: Agenda Item 05 - Appendix 1 - Draft Annual Report & Accounts 2025 2026
findings.headline: The 2025/26 internal audit of the Fund's administration function gave full (absolute) assurance
findings.detail: The paper says the Head of Audit and Procurement provided full (absolute) assurance that the internal control environment was sound. It also says no significant governance issues relating specifically to the Fund were reported in 2025/26.
findings.matters: A clean internal audit opinion on a pension administration function is a control result that finance directors at other councils can compare with their own audit outcomes.
findings.figures: Full (absolute) assurance; no significant governance issues reported in 2025/26

findings.paper_title: Agenda Item 05 - Appendix 1 - Draft Annual Report & Accounts 2025 2026
findings.headline: The Fund's net assets were £5.05bn at 31 March 2026, with £186.169m paid to pensioners and £188.111m of total contributions
findings.detail: The overview table shows 69,078 scheme members alongside net assets of the Fund, payments to pensioners and total contributions for the year. The paper gives these figures without further commentary in the overview.
findings.matters: Net assets against annual pension payments and contributions show the scale of the Fund's cash flows, which a finance director at another council can use as a benchmark.
findings.figures: Net assets £5.05bn; payments to pensioners £186.169m; total contributions £188.111m; 69,078 scheme members

findings.paper_title: Agenda Item 05 - Appendix 1 - Draft Annual Report & Accounts 2025 2026
findings.headline: Employer contribution rates reduced for many scheme employers following the 2025 valuation
findings.detail: The paper states that the improved funding position enabled contribution rates to be reduced for many scheme employers. The reduction is said to depend on each employer's individual circumstances.
findings.matters: Employer contribution rates are a recurring cost for councils and other scheme employers, so a finance director at another council can compare what happened to rates after a valuation with a surplus.
findings.quote: reduced for many scheme employers, subject to their individual circumstances.
